title: Limit acyclicity before and after coefficient restriction
statement: Fix a prime l, finite normed extensions E,F of Q_l, an embedding i:E→F and a scheme W. Let e identify source coefficient restriction of F-systems followed by source completed-tower restriction with target completed-tower restriction followed by termwise restriction along the completed coefficient map. For every K-injective F-system complex I, the universal right-derived inverse-limit unit is invertible both on its restricted completed F-tower and on the completed E-tower of its coefficient restriction. Neither restricted tower is required to be K-injective.

source.place: Tags 0D6E and 0941; agent-formulated normalization subargument of compact-support realization Step 11.

proof.text: For a tower X whose K-injective resolution j remains a quasi-isomorphism after ordinary limit, naturality of the actual derived-limit unit along j proves that its component at X is invertible: the other unit is invertible on a K-injective, and both localized resolution maps are invertible.
Apply the proved coefficient restriction acyclicity theorem to the underlying completed F-tower of I.

Use the exact sequence/strict-system equivalence. Compose the completed E→F coefficient map with the F projection cone. The generic restriction tower for this composite cone agrees with the F restriction tower followed by completed scalar restriction, by the identity on sections and the definition of the restricted action. The supplied e identifies it with the E-tower of the coefficient-restricted system. Generic restricted-system resolution acyclicity says that ordinary limit sends any K-injective resolution of this tower to a quasi-isomorphism. Apply the first step.

proof_origin: G1: proved from the existing restricted-system resolution acyclicity theorem, using the exact strict-system equivalence and the composite completed coefficient cone. Naturality of the actual right-derived unit turns the resulting limit quasi-isomorphisms into invertible unit components. No new sorry.

lean.statement:
theorem coefficientRestrictionLimitAcyclicity
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E F : Type u) [NormedField E] [NormedField F]
    [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[l] E] [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[l] F]
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] F]
    (i : E →ₐ[ℚ_[l]] F) (W : Scheme.{u})
    (e : systemRestriction l E F i W ⋙ coefficientSequenceRestriction.{u, u} l E W ≅
      coefficientSequenceRestriction.{u, u} l F W ⋙
        (Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ (scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l F W)
          (scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E W)).obj
          (pbcRestrict (completedCoefficientMap.{u, u} l E F i W)))
    (I : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules.{u, u} l F W) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] :
    IsIso ((rightUnit (lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l F W) ⥤
        scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l F W)).app
      (((coefficientSequenceRestriction.{u, u} l F W).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I)) ∧
    IsIso ((rightUnit (lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E W) ⥤
        scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E W)).app
      (((coefficientSequenceRestriction.{u, u} l E W).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
        (((systemRestriction l E F i W).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I)))
